Salvatore Sanfilippo makes a narrow terminology argument: models trained on outputs from DeepSeek R1 should be identified as distilled models, not treated as R1 itself.

## Key Ideas

- R1 and its distilled models differ in size, base model, and training route. Sanfilippo contrasts reinforcement learning for R1 with supervised fine-tuning of smaller Llama- and Qwen-based models. [00:00:00]
- In the account given here, R1 generates a large set of outputs that becomes training data for the smaller models. Those models should therefore be described as distilled through R1 rather than as members of the same model. [00:01:02]

## Practical Implications

- Name a distilled release with both its underlying model family and its relationship to the teacher model.
- Distinguish generation of training data from inheritance of architecture, weights, or training method when comparing model releases.

## Questions and Tensions

- The short transcript argues for precise naming but does not define a complete naming convention for checkpoints that combine several training stages.
- The training description is compressed; use the original model documentation before relying on it for detailed implementation claims.
